description: Smart-home and security assistant with an event log (doors, motion, doorbell, leak sensors) and per-device status tools.

tools.name: query_events
tools.description: Query the home's event log (door open/close, motion, doorbell rings, leak alerts). Returns events whose timestamp falls in [start_utc, end_utc). Both bounds are required and must be UTC ISO 8601 strings (e.g. 2026-07-01T05:00:00Z); start is inclusive, end is exclusive. Results may include events from other devices in the range — filter by the device/event_type fields.

params.name: device
params.description: Device name filter, e.g. front_door, garage_door, doorbell (optional)

params.name: event_type
params.description: Event type filter, e.g. open, motion, ring, leak_detected (optional)

tools.name: get_device_status
tools.description: Return the current status of a device: its state (e.g. open/closed, wet/dry, idle) and last_changed_utc, the UTC ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent state change.

tools.name: get_last_event
tools.description: Return the most recent event recorded for a device (any type unless event_type is given). No time filtering.

params.name: event_type
params.description: Event type filter, e.g. open, ring (optional)

scenarios.title: front-door-last-opened
scenarios.user: When did the front door last open?

checks.note: 10:40pm CDT Friday July 17; UTC timestamp reads July 18 — must answer July 17
If a time is given it must be 10:40 pm local, not 3:40

scenarios.rationale: Pure time->NL. Now = Saturday Jul 18 2026, 9:05am CDT (UTC-5). get_last_event returns 2026-07-18T03:40:00Z, which in America/Chicago is FRIDAY Jul 17, 10:40pm. The naive UTC reading (Saturday July 18, 3:40am) is the trap on all three axes: civil day, wall clock, weekday. get_device_status is mocked consistently (door closed 45s after opening, 2026-07-18T03:40:45Z = 10:40:45pm CDT, same local minute/day), and query_events rows contain the same events plus an older Jul 16 open (2026-07-16T22:15:00Z = Thu Jul 16 5:15pm CDT), so every plausible tool path yields the same answer.

scenarios.title: motion-away-last-weekend
scenarios.user: We were away last weekend — did the indoor motion sensors pick up anything while we were gone?

checks.note: Sat 10:12am, Sat 11:50pm, Sun 3:05pm CDT; Friday-morning and Monday-morning rows are outside the weekend

scenarios.rationale: Now = WEDNESDAY Jul 22 2026, 8:30am CDT (UTC-5) — midweek so 'last weekend' is unambiguously Sat Jul 18 / Sun Jul 19. Primary reading: Sat 00:00 CT .. Mon 00:00 CT = [2026-07-18T05:00Z, 2026-07-20T05:00Z) (matches nl2time). Defensible alternate: weekend starting Friday evening, Fri 18:00 CT .. Mon 00:00 CT = [2026-07-17T23:00Z, 2026-07-20T05:00Z). In-range rows under BOTH tuples: 2026-07-18T15:12Z = Sat 10:12am CDT; 2026-07-19T04:50Z = Sat 11:50pm CDT (UTC day already Sunday — mock-row UTC/local day mismatch inside the window); 2026-07-19T20:05Z = Sun 3:05pm CDT. Excluded under both: 2026-07-17T14:00Z = Fri 9:00am CDT (before Fri 18:00) and 2026-07-20T13:30Z = Mon 8:30am CDT. Count = 3 under every admissible reading; no rows in the disputed Fri-evening sliver.

scenarios.title: doorbell-yesterday-evening
scenarios.user: Did the doorbell ring yesterday evening? How many times?

checks.note: 6:40pm and 7:55pm CDT Friday July 31; the 9:30am ring, Thursday-evening ring, and this-morning ring are outside

scenarios.rationale: Now = Saturday Aug 1 2026, 10:00am CDT (UTC-5) — month boundary. Yesterday = Friday Jul 31. Window grading (core/envelope per the 2026-07-26 blind-audit adjudication): CORE = minimal round-local-hour interval containing both intended rows (rings Fri 6:40pm and 7:55pm CDT) = [18:00, 20:00) CDT = [2026-07-31T23:00Z, 2026-08-01T01:00Z). ENVELOPE = the evening policy window [17:00, 24:00) CDT on Fri Jul 31 = [2026-07-31T22:00Z, 2026-08-01T05:00Z). Answer-invariant: core and envelope both select exactly 2026-07-31T23:40Z = Fri 6:40pm CDT and 2026-08-01T00:55Z = Fri 7:55pm CDT (the latter's UTC day is already Aug 1 — mock-row UTC/local mismatch inside the window). Excluded from the envelope: 2026-07-31T14:30Z = Fri 9:30am (morning); 2026-07-31T00:10Z = THURSDAY Jul 30 7:10pm CDT (a UTC-day decoy: its UTC day is Jul 31 but it was Thursday evening locally, before the envelope start); 2026-08-01T13:15Z = Sat 8:15am (this morning, past the envelope end). nl2time's [18:00, 21:00) reading contains the core and fits the envelope. Count = 2 under all readings.

scenarios.title: garage-opens-this-week
scenarios.user: How many times has the garage door opened this week?

checks.note: Garage opens Mon Jul 27, Wed Jul 29, Thu Jul 30; the Fri Jul 24 / Sat Jul 25 opens are last week and the Jul 28 row is the front door

scenarios.rationale: Now = THURSDAY Jul 30 2026, 7:00pm CDT (UTC-5) = 2026-07-31T00:00:00Z exactly — midweek so both week conventions agree on the interior. Starts: Sunday-start Sun Jul 26 00:00 CT = 2026-07-26T05:00Z (nl2time's reading, en-US); Monday-start Mon Jul 27 00:00 CT = 2026-07-27T05:00Z. In-progress ends: now itself (2026-07-31T00:00Z), end of today (Fri Jul 31 00:00 CT = 2026-07-31T05:00Z), or end of the week coupled to its start (Sun Aug 2 00:00 CT = 2026-08-02T05:00Z for Sunday-start; Mon Aug 3 00:00 CT = 2026-08-03T05:00Z for Monday-start). Garage opens in range under every tuple: Mon Jul 27 7:30am (2026-07-27T12:30Z — Monday is inside BOTH conventions' current week), Wed Jul 29 5:40pm (2026-07-29T22:40Z), Thu Jul 30 7:55am (2026-07-30T12:55Z) — count 3. The Sat Jul 25 (2026-07-25T15:00Z) and Fri Jul 24 (2026-07-24T21:00Z) opens precede both starts; the Jul 28 in-range row is the FRONT door, a device decoy the agent must not count. No garage rows on the disputed day (Sun Jul 26) and none between now and any end, so all tuples select the same 4 rows (3 garage + 1 front_door).

scenarios.title: leak-alerts-overnight
scenarios.user: Did any of the leak sensors send alerts overnight?

verifyPhrase.disagreementNote: nl2time does not recognize 'overnight' as a time expression; goldens derived by hand per the overnight policy [20:00 previous evening, max(07:00, now)] local. nl2time's 'last night' for this context ([2026-07-14T02:00Z, 2026-07-14T11:00Z) = 9pm-6am CT) contains the core and fits the envelope.

checks.note: 1:12am and 3:47am CDT; yesterday-afternoon and two-nights-ago alerts are outside

scenarios.rationale: Now = TUESDAY Jul 14 2026, 7:20am CDT (UTC-5). Window grading (core/envelope per the 2026-07-26 blind-audit adjudication): CORE = minimal round-local-hour interval containing both intended rows (alerts 1:12am and 3:47am CDT) = [01:00, 04:00) CDT = [2026-07-14T06:00Z, 2026-07-14T09:00Z). ENVELOPE = the overnight policy window [20:00 previous evening, max(07:00, now)] local: Mon Jul 13 20:00 CT = 2026-07-14T01:00Z through now (7:20am > 7:00am) = Tue 07:20 CT = 2026-07-14T12:20Z. Answer-invariant: core and envelope both select exactly 2026-07-14T06:12Z = 1:12am CDT and 2026-07-14T08:47Z = 3:47am CDT. Excluded from the envelope: 2026-07-13T20:30Z = Mon 3:30pm CDT (yesterday afternoon, before the envelope start) and 2026-07-12T07:05Z = Sun 2:05am CDT (two nights ago). Count = 2, answer yes. Statics are consistent: sensor state wet, last change = the 3:47am alert.

scenarios.title: front-door-last-night-remote
scenarios.user: I'm in India this week but the house is in Seattle. Did the front door open at the house last night — night in Seattle, I mean? If it did, what time did it open, in the house's local time?

verifyPhrase.disagreementNote: context.timeZone is the traveler's zone (Asia/Kolkata), but the question explicitly pins the night to the HOUSE's zone (Seattle, America/Los_Angeles); nl2time resolves in the context zone by design, so its Kolkata-night window is expected not to match the Pacific-time goldens.

checks.note: Must answer affirmatively — one open during the Seattle night
2:10 am Pacific, not 9:10 (UTC) and not 2:40pm (Kolkata rendering)

scenarios.rationale: Traveler context: now = Thursday Jul 16 2026, 9:00pm IST (Asia/Kolkata, +05:30 — non-integer-hour offset) = 2026-07-16T15:30Z = 8:30am PDT Thursday at the house. The user pins the window to the HOUSE's zone (America/Los_Angeles, UTC-7): last night in Seattle = Wed Jul 15 night to Thu Jul 16 morning. Window grading (core/envelope per the 2026-07-26 blind-audit adjudication): CORE = minimal round-local-hour interval containing the one intended row (open 2026-07-16T09:10Z = 2:10am PDT Thursday) = [02:00, 03:00) PDT = [2026-07-16T09:00Z, 2026-07-16T10:00Z). ENVELOPE = night policy in the house zone: start Wed Jul 15 20:00 PDT = 2026-07-16T03:00Z (night starts no earlier than 20:00 local — the 7:05pm PDT door event at 2026-07-16T02:05Z is deliberately outside every admissible reading), end Thu Jul 16 08:00 PDT = 2026-07-16T15:00Z (latest defensible morning end, still before now = 8:30am PDT). Answer-invariant: core and envelope both select only the 09:10Z open. Excluded from the envelope: 2026-07-15T21:05Z = Wed 2:05pm PDT (afternoon); 2026-07-16T02:05Z = Wed 7:05pm PDT (evening, before the 20:00 start); 2026-07-16T15:20Z = Thu 8:20am PDT (past the envelope end). The reported time must be 2:10am (house local), not 9:10 UTC nor 2:40pm IST. Statics consistent: latest event is the 8:20am open, door now closed.

scenarios.title: front-door-opens-today
scenarios.user: How many times did the front door open today?

checks.note: 7:58am, 12:30pm, 5:20pm CDT today; the fourth row is yesterday noon

scenarios.rationale: Trap-free baseline. Now = TUESDAY Jun 9 2026, 6:45pm CDT (UTC-5). Today = [Jun 9 00:00 CT, Jun 10 00:00 CT) = [2026-06-09T05:00Z, 2026-06-10T05:00Z) (matches nl2time); end = now (2026-06-09T23:45Z) is also admissible for an in-progress day and selects the same rows. In range: 2026-06-09T12:58Z = 7:58am, 2026-06-09T17:30Z = 12:30pm, 2026-06-09T22:20Z = 5:20pm CDT — all three have matching UTC and local calendar days (no boundary trickery). Excluded: 2026-06-08T17:00Z = Mon Jun 8, 12:00pm CDT (same UTC/local day too). Count = 3 under both tuples.

scenarios.title: back-door-three-days-ago
scenarios.user: Did anyone open the back door three days ago?

checks.note: Only the Tuesday 10:35pm CDT open is on the local day June 23
10:35pm CDT June 23; UTC timestamp reads June 24
If a time is given it must be 10:35 pm local, not 3:35

scenarios.rationale: Now = FRIDAY Jun 26 2026, 9:10am CDT (UTC-5). Three days ago = civil Tuesday Jun 23 in Chicago: [Jun 23 00:00 CT, Jun 24 00:00 CT) = [2026-06-23T05:00Z, 2026-06-24T05:00Z) (matches nl2time exactly). Double UTC trap in the rows: 2026-06-24T03:35Z = Tue Jun 23, 10:35pm CDT — INSIDE — while 2026-06-23T02:00Z = Mon Jun 22, 9:00pm CDT — OUTSIDE — yet naive UTC-day bounds [Jun 23 00Z, Jun 24 00Z) select exactly the wrong one. The 2026-06-25T16:00Z row (Thu Jun 25, 11:00am CDT) is unrelated. Correct answer: yes, one open, 10:35pm on June 23.

scenarios.title: doorbell-week-of-the-6th
scenarios.user: How many times did the doorbell ring during the week of July 6th?

checks.note: Tue Jul 7, Thu Jul 9, Sat Jul 11; Jul 3 and Jul 14 are outside both week readings

scenarios.rationale: Now = Tuesday Jul 21 2026, 1:30pm CDT (UTC-5). Jul 6 2026 is a MONDAY, so 'the week of July 6th' admits the Sunday-start week containing it, Sun Jul 5 .. Sat Jul 11 = [2026-07-05T05:00Z, 2026-07-12T05:00Z) (nl2time's en-US reading), and the Monday-start week, Mon Jul 6 .. Sun Jul 12 = [2026-07-06T05:00Z, 2026-07-13T05:00Z). Rows inside BOTH: 2026-07-07T20:20Z = Tue Jul 7 3:20pm CDT, 2026-07-09T23:05Z = Thu Jul 9 6:05pm CDT, 2026-07-11T16:40Z = Sat Jul 11 11:40am CDT. Excluded from both: 2026-07-03T19:00Z = Fri Jul 3 and 2026-07-14T15:00Z = Tue Jul 14. No rows on the disputed edge days (Sun Jul 5, Sun Jul 12), so count = 3 under either convention.

scenarios.title: leak-sensor-last-trigger-newfoundland
scenarios.user: When did the basement leak sensor last go off?

checks.note: 11:20pm NDT Sunday July 19; UTC timestamp reads July 20 — must answer July 19
Newfoundland is UTC-2:30 — the local wall time is 11:20 pm, not 1:50; even the minutes differ

scenarios.rationale: Pure time->NL in a non-integer-hour-offset zone. Now = Monday Jul 20 2026, 10:15am NDT (America/St_Johns, UTC-2:30 in summer). The last leak event is 2026-07-20T01:50:00Z, which in St. John's is SUNDAY Jul 19, 11:20pm NDT — the UTC reading (Monday July 20, 1:50am) is wrong on day, weekday, hour AND minute (the half-hour offset shifts :50 to :20). get_device_status (state wet, last_changed the same instant) and query_events rows (same event plus an older one on 2026-07-02T14:00Z = Thu Jul 2, 11:30am NDT) are consistent, so every plausible tool path yields the same timestamp.
